authoritativeScope.apCoreScope: AP Precalculus Units 1-3 before the AP examination; Unit 4 remains optional supplemental enrichment.

transferProtocol.exceptionalGate: End of Week 17 with AP Unit 1-2 catch-up evidence and AP-pace independence

criteria.Evidence: Grade 9 readiness evidence + common Grade 10 diagnostic.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Correct obvious misplacements immediately before substantive AP content accumulates.

criteria.Evidence: Readiness Gateway 1 about 85%+ overall, about 80%+ on AP-extension items, all critical prerequisites secure, strong independent work; complete a short AP Unit 1 catch-up check if needed.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Transfer to Path A at the start of AP Unit 2. This is the cleanest in-year movement point.

criteria.Evidence: Very high cumulative mastery; AP-extension performance at AP pace; completion of AP Unit 1-2 catch-up modules; scheduling/AP exam implications resolved.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Transfer only when evidence shows the student can enter AP Unit 3 without sacrificing understanding. Otherwise remain in Path B and target Grade 11 AP.

criteria.Evidence: Continue common stretch tasks and AP-style benchmarks, but normally avoid changing sections late.
criteria.Recommended Decision: Protect continuity. A strong Path B student should finish the year as an exceptionally well-prepared Grade 11 AP Precalculus student.

transferProtocol.note: Important: Transfer decisions should use strand evidence, AP-pace independence, and completion of catch-up content—not only a course average. A student with a high average but unresolved factoring, function, or trigonometry gaps is likely to struggle after transfer.

pathA.title: Grade 10 Path A - AP Precalculus
pathA.destination: Complete AP Precalculus Units 1-3, the cumulative AP review/mock package, and selected calculus-bridge extensions E.1-E.4.

units.title: Polynomial and Rational Functions
units.intent: Develop covariational reasoning and polynomial/rational function analysis through graphical, numerical, analytical, and contextual representations.
units.phaseFocus: AP Topics 1.1-1.14; covariation and rates of change; polynomial/rational structure; zeros, end behavior, asymptotes/holes; transformations; model selection/construction.
units.implementationEvidence: Common Gateway A1 at end of unit; prerequisite micro-repair embedded, not a separate slow unit.

lessons.title: Change in Tandem
subtopics: Covariation; input/output quantities; increasing/decreasing behavior; contextual change; representation matching.
learningOutcomes: Describe how two quantities vary together; identify intervals of increase/decrease from multiple representations; communicate covariation precisely.

lessons.title: Rates of Change
subtopics: Average rate of change; secant slope; units; interval comparison; estimating local change from data/graphs.
learningOutcomes: Calculate and interpret average rates of change; compare rates across intervals; connect numerical rates to graph steepness and context.

lessons.title: Rates of Change in Linear and Quadratic Functions
subtopics: Constant vs changing rate; first/second differences; linear vs quadratic behavior; contextual interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Distinguish constant and changing rates; use first/second differences to classify behavior; justify a model family from rate structure.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions and Rates of Change
subtopics: Polynomial degree and rate patterns; local/global behavior; tables/graphs; regression-supported exploration.
learningOutcomes: Describe how rates change for polynomial functions; connect degree to qualitative behavior; interpret polynomial change in context.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions and Complex Zeros
subtopics: Real/complex zeros; conjugate pairs; factor form; multiplicity; graph connection.
learningOutcomes: Determine zeros from polynomial structure; use complex conjugate relationships for real-coefficient polynomials; connect real zeros/multiplicity to graph behavior.

lessons.title: Polynomial Functions and End Behavior
subtopics: Leading term; degree parity; sign of leading coefficient; end behavior notation; global graph shape.
learningOutcomes: Determine end behavior analytically and graphically; use the leading term to predict behavior; connect equivalent forms to end behavior.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and End Behavior
subtopics: Degree comparison; horizontal/oblique end behavior; quotient interpretation; long-run model behavior.
learningOutcomes: Determine rational end behavior; identify an appropriate end-behavior model/asymptote; explain how numerator/denominator degree controls long-run behavior.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Zeros
subtopics: Zeros from numerator; domain restrictions; canceled factors; sign behavior.
learningOutcomes: Identify zeros of rational functions correctly; distinguish a zero from an excluded value; solve rational equations with domain awareness.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Vertical Asymptotes
subtopics: Denominator zeros after simplification; one-sided behavior; sign charts; graphical/numerical evidence.
learningOutcomes: Locate vertical asymptotes; describe one-sided behavior; justify asymptotes using simplified structure and nearby values.

lessons.title: Rational Functions and Holes
subtopics: Common factors; removable discontinuities; hole coordinates; equivalent expressions vs functions.
learningOutcomes: Identify holes and their coordinates; explain why cancellation does not restore the excluded input; distinguish holes from asymptotes.

lessons.title: Equivalent Representations of Polynomial and Rational Expressions
subtopics: Expanded/factored forms; polynomial division; partial structural rewriting where useful; information revealed by form.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite expressions into strategically useful equivalent forms; select a form that reveals zeros, end behavior, or local features; verify equivalence and restrictions.

lessons.title: Transformations of Functions
subtopics: Translations; reflections; vertical/horizontal scaling; parameter effects; transformations across function families.
learningOutcomes: Construct transformed functions; predict graph changes from parameters; recover an equation from a transformed graph or contextual condition.

lessons.title: Function Model Selection and Assumption Articulation
subtopics: Regression candidates; residuals; data window; assumptions; interpolation/extrapolation; model limitations.
learningOutcomes: Select a defensible polynomial/rational model; use residual/context evidence; articulate assumptions and limitations with precise language.

lessons.title: Function Model Construction and Application
subtopics: Build models from conditions/data; regression; parameter interpretation; solve and apply model outputs.
learningOutcomes: Construct a function model; interpret parameters and numerical results; use the model to answer contextual questions and assess reasonableness.

units.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Functions
units.intent: Develop multiplicative-change reasoning, inverse/composition fluency, and data-modeling skills with exponential and logarithmic functions.
units.phaseFocus: AP Topics 2.1-2.15; sequences; exponential change; composition/inverses; logarithms; equations/inequalities; context/data modeling; semi-log plots.
units.implementationEvidence: Common Gateway A2; cumulative AP-style FRQ and calculator/non-calculator practice.

lessons.title: Change in Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
subtopics: Discrete functions; common difference/ratio; explicit forms; additive vs multiplicative change.
learningOutcomes: Represent arithmetic/geometric sequences as functions of whole-number inputs; interpret common difference/ratio; compare additive and multiplicative change.

lessons.title: Change in Linear and Exponential Functions
subtopics: Continuous extensions of sequences; constant difference vs constant ratio; growth factor; rate patterns.
learningOutcomes: Compare linear and exponential change; construct continuous function models related to sequences; explain why multiplicative change produces exponential behavior.

lessons.title: Exponential Functions
subtopics: Initial value; base/growth factor; domain/range; asymptote; monotonicity; transformations.
learningOutcomes: Describe key characteristics of exponential functions; construct an exponential function from conditions; interpret parameters in context.

lessons.title: Exponential Function Manipulation
subtopics: Exponent laws; equivalent bases; rational exponents; isolating parameters; strategically equivalent forms.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite exponential expressions into useful equivalent forms; apply exponent laws fluently; reveal growth factor, initial value, or comparison structure.

lessons.title: Exponential Function Context and Data Modeling
subtopics: Exponential regression; growth/decay; percent rate; doubling/halving interpretation; residuals.
learningOutcomes: Fit and interpret exponential models; convert between growth factor and percent rate; apply the model and evaluate fit.

lessons.title: Competing Function Model Validation
subtopics: Compare linear/quadratic/exponential models; residual plots; contextual plausibility; model selection.
learningOutcomes: Compare competing models using data, residuals, and context; justify a choice; identify when a model should be rejected.

lessons.title: Composition of Functions
subtopics: Composition notation; domains; process interpretation; multiple representations; modeling chains.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate and construct compositions; determine valid domains; interpret a composition as sequential processes in context.

lessons.title: Inverse Functions
subtopics: One-to-one behavior; inverse notation; graph reflection; domain/range exchange; verification by composition.
learningOutcomes: Determine and verify inverses; restrict domains when needed; connect inverse graphs and swapped domain/range.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Expressions
subtopics: Definition of logarithm; convert exponential/log forms; common/natural logs; exact values.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite between exponential and logarithmic forms; evaluate logarithms from known powers; interpret a logarithm as an exponent.

lessons.title: Inverses of Exponential Functions
subtopics: Logarithms as inverse functions; inverse graphs; domain/range/asymptotes; composition identities.
learningOutcomes: Construct inverse relationships for exponential functions; use logarithms to undo exponential processes; connect graphs and domains.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Functions
subtopics: Characteristics; transformations; vertical asymptote; increasing/decreasing behavior; multiple representations.
learningOutcomes: Describe and graph logarithmic functions; interpret parameters; identify domain, range, intercept behavior, and asymptote.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Function Manipulation
subtopics: Product/quotient/power properties; change of base; equivalent forms; restrictions.
learningOutcomes: Expand/condense logarithmic expressions; use change of base; preserve domain restrictions while rewriting.

lessons.title: Exponential and Logarithmic Equations and Inequalities
subtopics: Common-base methods; logarithms; exact/numerical solutions; inequality reasoning; extraneous/domain checks.
learningOutcomes: Solve exponential/logarithmic equations and inequalities analytically or numerically; check domain conditions; interpret solutions in context.

lessons.title: Logarithmic Function Context and Data Modeling
subtopics: Logarithmic regression; diminishing growth contexts; parameter interpretation; residuals.
learningOutcomes: Fit and interpret logarithmic models; compare with alternative models; use the model to make and qualify predictions.

lessons.title: Semi-log Plots
subtopics: Log-scaled axis; exponential linearization; slope/intercept meaning in transformed scale; model validation.
learningOutcomes: Determine whether exponential behavior is plausible from a semi-log plot; construct/interpret linearization; connect transformed slope/intercept to exponential parameters.

units.title: Trigonometric and Polar Functions
units.intent: Develop periodic-function, trigonometric-identity, and polar-function reasoning with strong modeling and multiple-representation fluency.
units.phaseFocus: AP Topics 3.1-3.15; periodic phenomena; trig functions/graphs; sinusoidal modeling; inverse trig; equations/identities; polar coordinates/functions/rates.
units.implementationEvidence: Common Gateway A3; full Units 1-3 cumulative benchmark.

lessons.title: Periodic Phenomena
subtopics: Periodicity in context; cycles; period; repeated patterns; graphing a cycle; input/output interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Recognize periodic relationships; construct a graph from one cycle; interpret period and repeated behavior in context.

lessons.title: Sine, Cosine, and Tangent
subtopics: Angles in standard position; radian measure; unit-circle definitions; signs by quadrant; tangent as ratio.
learningOutcomes: Define sine/cosine/tangent for angles; connect right-triangle and unit-circle meanings; determine signs and basic characteristics.

lessons.title: Sine and Cosine Function Values
subtopics: Exact unit-circle values; reference angles; symmetry; degrees/radians; technology-supported values.
learningOutcomes: Determine exact or approximate sine/cosine values; use symmetry/reference angles; move accurately between degree and radian measures.

lessons.title: Sine and Cosine Function Graphs
subtopics: Domain/range; period; zeros; extrema; midline; graph from unit-circle behavior.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret sine/cosine graphs; identify key features; connect graph locations to unit-circle coordinates.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Functions
subtopics: Amplitude; period; midline; phase/shift ideas; parameter interpretation; equivalent sinusoidal descriptions.
learningOutcomes: Analyze sinusoidal functions from equations/graphs; determine key parameters; write a sinusoidal function from features.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Function Transformations
subtopics: Horizontal/vertical shifts; amplitude/period changes; reflections; parameter effects.
learningOutcomes: Construct transformed sinusoidal functions; recover equations from graphs; explain parameter effects precisely.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Function Context and Data Modeling
subtopics: Periodic data; sinusoidal regression; parameter meaning; assumptions; residuals.
learningOutcomes: Build a sinusoidal model from context/data; interpret amplitude, midline, period, and shift; judge fit and limitations.

lessons.title: The Tangent Function
subtopics: Graph; period; zeros; vertical asymptotes; transformations; contextual angle relationships.
learningOutcomes: Describe and graph tangent functions; identify asymptotes/period; solve or model accessible tangent relationships.

lessons.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
subtopics: Principal-value domains/ranges; arcsin/arccos/arctan; inverse graphs; compositions.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate inverse trig functions; use principal-value restrictions correctly; solve for angles and interpret inverse-trig outputs.

lessons.title: Trigonometric Equations and Inequalities
subtopics: General solutions over intervals; graph/algebra methods; inverse trig; periodic solution sets; inequalities.
learningOutcomes: Solve trig equations/inequalities on specified domains; use periodicity to generate solutions; verify graphically/numerically.

lessons.title: The Secant, Cosecant, and Cotangent Functions
subtopics: Reciprocal definitions; domains; asymptotes; graphs; relationships to sine/cosine/tangent.
learningOutcomes: Construct and analyze reciprocal trig functions; locate zeros/asymptotes; connect their graphs to the primary trig functions.

lessons.title: Equivalent Representations of Trigonometric Functions
subtopics: Pythagorean identities; sine/cosine sum identities; difference/double-angle consequences; identity verification; solving with equivalent forms.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite trigonometric expressions using required identities; verify identities; choose an equivalent form that simplifies an equation or reveals information.

lessons.title: Trigonometry and Polar Coordinates
subtopics: Polar system; multiple representations of a point; rectangular-polar conversion; complex numbers in polar form.
learningOutcomes: Locate points in both systems; convert coordinates accurately; explain nonuniqueness of polar coordinates; connect complex-plane and polar representations.

lessons.title: Polar Function Graphs
subtopics: r=f(theta); signed radius; domain restrictions; tables/technology; common polar behavior.
learningOutcomes: Construct and interpret polar graphs; connect changes in theta and r to motion in the plane; use domain restrictions to display intended portions.

lessons.title: Rates of Change in Polar Functions
subtopics: Increasing/decreasing signed radius; distance from origin; relative extrema; average rate of change of r with respect to theta.
learningOutcomes: Describe polar graph characteristics; compute/interpret average rate of change in radius per radian; connect extrema to relative distance from the origin.

units.title: Selected Post-Exam Calculus Bridge
units.intent: Use remaining instructional time on content with direct value for later calculus, rather than on low-priority topics.
units.phaseFocus: Selected parametric functions, planar motion, implicit relations, vector-valued thinking, advanced function analysis; no matrix-heavy core unless locally required.
units.implementationEvidence: Prepares later AP Calculus AB/BC without displacing tested AP Precalculus content.

lessons.title: Parametric Functions
subtopics: x(t), y(t); parameter domain; eliminating parameter when appropriate; orientation.
learningOutcomes: Represent planar curves parametrically; move between parametric and Cartesian descriptions when feasible; interpret the parameter.

lessons.title: Planar Motion with Parametric Functions
subtopics: Position components; tables/graphs; direction and time; contextual motion.
learningOutcomes: Interpret parametric position models; describe motion and orientation; connect component changes to overall movement.

lessons.title: Implicit Relations and Function Restrictions
subtopics: Implicitly defined curves; local function behavior; solving for branches; domain restrictions.
learningOutcomes: Interpret implicit relations; determine when a relation can represent y as a function locally; identify branches and restrictions.

lessons.title: Vector-Valued Function Preview
subtopics: 2D vectors; magnitude/direction; component form; r(t)=<x(t),y(t)>; connection to BC calculus vocabulary.
learningOutcomes: Represent motion with vectors; connect parametric and vector-valued notation; interpret components, magnitude, and direction conceptually.

requiredPackages.title: Cumulative AP Review & Exam Preparation
requiredPackages.focus: Spiral review by skill and representation; timed mixed MCQ/FRQ; regression/modeling; calculator fluency; error-driven reteaching.
requiredPackages.evidence: At least two full mock cycles plus targeted re-teach by strand.

supplementalUnits.title: Functions Involving Parameters, Vectors, and Matrices
supplementalUnits.classification: Supplemental/enrichment; not part of the required Path A lesson count

pathB.title: Grade 10 Path B - AP Readiness / Transition
pathB.destination: Full readiness to enter AP Precalculus in Grade 11, with evidence-based transfer gates into Path A.

units.title: Diagnostic & Precision Repair
units.intent: Create an evidence-based starting point and repair only the prerequisite skills that would block progress.
units.phaseFocus: Common diagnostic; algebra repair; function notation; calculator/non-calculator habits; individualized flex groups.

lessons.title: Common Entry Diagnostic
subtopics: Linear/quadratic fluency; functions; factoring; exponents/radicals; systems; right-triangle trig; graph reading.
learningOutcomes: Identify strand-level strengths/gaps; demonstrate calculator/non-calculator fluency; set targeted mastery goals.

lessons.title: Algebra Precision Repair
subtopics: Fractions; signs; exponent laws; equation steps; factoring basics; notation.
learningOutcomes: Execute core algebra accurately; identify and correct common errors; explain why algebraic transformations preserve equivalence.

lessons.title: Function Notation & Representation Repair
subtopics: f(x); domain/range; graph/table/formula/context; interval notation; rate language.
learningOutcomes: Interpret function notation and domains; move among representations; use correct interval and rate-of-change language.

units.title: Polynomial & Rational Foundations
units.intent: Develop the same function families as AP Unit 1, but with more time for prerequisite algebra and guided reasoning.
units.phaseFocus: Rates of change; quadratic mastery; polynomial operations/factoring/zeros/end behavior; rational expressions/functions; zeros/asymptotes/holes; transformations/modeling.
units.implementationEvidence: Parallel to AP Unit 1 at scaffolded depth. Transfer Gate 1 at end of Week 9.

lessons.title: Linear and Quadratic Rates of Change
subtopics: Slope; average rate of change; first/second differences; quadratic forms.
learningOutcomes: Compare constant/changing rates; compute average rates; identify linear vs quadratic behavior from representations.

lessons.title: Quadratic Mastery Check & Repair
subtopics: Factoring; completing square; quadratic formula; discriminant; inequalities.
learningOutcomes: Solve quadratics by multiple methods; choose an efficient method; solve quadratic inequalities and classify roots.

lessons.title: Polynomial Operations and Factoring
subtopics: Operations; special products; grouping; cubes; structure.
learningOutcomes: Perform polynomial operations; factor strategically; verify factorization and use it to solve equations.

lessons.title: Polynomial Zeros, Multiplicity & Complex Numbers
subtopics: Real/complex roots; conjugates; factor form; multiplicity; graph behavior.
learningOutcomes: Connect zeros/factors/intercepts; use complex conjugates; predict crossing/touching behavior from multiplicity.

lessons.title: Polynomial End Behavior & Graph Construction
subtopics: Degree; leading term; end behavior; intercepts; turning behavior; regression preview.
learningOutcomes: Predict end behavior; sketch graphs from algebraic structure; interpret features in context.

lessons.title: Rational Expressions and Equations
subtopics: Restrictions; simplification; operations; rational equations; excluded values.
learningOutcomes: Simplify and solve rational expressions/equations with domain control; detect invalid/extraneous values.

lessons.title: Rational Functions: Zeros, Asymptotes and Holes
subtopics: Zeros; vertical/horizontal end behavior; holes; sign behavior; multiple representations.
learningOutcomes: Identify zeros/asymptotes/holes; explain each from algebraic structure; sketch and interpret rational graphs.

lessons.title: Transformations and Model Selection
subtopics: Function transformations; polynomial/rational models; regression/residual idea; assumptions.
learningOutcomes: Construct transformed functions; select a plausible model; state assumptions and limitations using evidence.

units.title: Exponential & Logarithmic Foundations
units.intent: Build full Algebra 2-level exponential/logarithmic fluency while mirroring the AP Unit 2 sequence.
units.phaseFocus: Sequences; exponent laws; exponential functions/modeling; composition/inverses; logarithms; exp/log equations; model comparison; regression.
units.implementationEvidence: Parallel to AP Unit 2. Transfer Gate 2 at end of Week 17 for exceptional candidates.

lessons.title: Arithmetic and Geometric Sequences
subtopics: Explicit/recursive rules; difference/ratio; discrete domains; sequence-to-function connection.
learningOutcomes: Write and interpret sequence rules; distinguish additive/multiplicative change; connect sequences to linear/exponential functions.

lessons.title: Exponent Laws and Rational Exponents
subtopics: Integer/rational exponents; radicals; equivalent forms; scientific notation as needed.
learningOutcomes: Apply exponent laws fluently; rewrite radicals and rational exponents; simplify expressions without sign/domain errors.

lessons.title: Exponential Functions and Transformations
subtopics: Initial value; growth factor; asymptote; domain/range; transformations.
learningOutcomes: Construct, graph, and interpret exponential functions; connect parameters to features; compare transformations.

lessons.title: Exponential Modeling
subtopics: Percent growth/decay; compound contexts; regression; residuals; doubling/halving.
learningOutcomes: Build exponential models; interpret growth factors/rates; evaluate model fit and make contextual predictions.

lessons.title: Composition and Inverse Functions
subtopics: Composition; one-to-one idea; inverse notation; graph reflection; domain restriction.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate compositions; determine/verify inverses; restrict domains when required; interpret inverse processes.

lessons.title: Logarithms as Inverses
subtopics: Exponential-log equivalence; common/natural logs; graphs; domain/range; asymptote.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite between forms; evaluate logarithms; connect log graphs to exponential inverses; identify domain restrictions.

lessons.title: Logarithm Properties
subtopics: Product/quotient/power properties; change of base; expanding/condensing.
learningOutcomes: Manipulate logarithmic expressions accurately; use change of base; preserve valid domains.

lessons.title: Exponential and Log Equations
subtopics: Common-base solving; logs; numerical methods; inequalities; checking.
learningOutcomes: Solve exponential/logarithmic equations; check domain; use technology appropriately when an exact algebraic solution is unavailable.

lessons.title: Comparing and Validating Models
subtopics: Linear/quadratic/exponential/log models; regression; residuals; informal semi-log interpretation.
learningOutcomes: Choose a model from evidence; compare residual behavior; explain why a model is plausible or not.

units.title: Trigonometric & Polar Foundations
units.intent: Build a strong trigonometric foundation so AP Unit 3 can be learned conceptually rather than as a first exposure.
units.phaseFocus: Radians/unit circle; sine/cosine/tangent values and graphs; sinusoidal models; inverse trig; equations; core identities; polar coordinates/graphs.
units.implementationEvidence: Builds complete entry readiness for AP Unit 3; end-of-unit readiness benchmark.

lessons.title: Radians, Standard Position & Unit Circle
subtopics: Degree-radian conversion; arc length concept; unit-circle coordinates; quadrants/reference angles.
learningOutcomes: Convert angle measures; locate angles in standard position; determine unit-circle coordinates and reference angles.

lessons.title: Sine, Cosine and Tangent Values
subtopics: Unit-circle definitions; exact values; signs; right-triangle connection; calculator values.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate trig functions exactly or approximately; connect right-triangle and unit-circle definitions; use quadrant reasoning.

lessons.title: Sine and Cosine Graphs
subtopics: Period; amplitude; midline; zeros/extrema; graph construction.
learningOutcomes: Graph and analyze sine/cosine; identify key features; connect graph behavior to the unit circle.

lessons.title: Sinusoidal Transformations and Modeling
subtopics: A sin(B(x-C))+D; parameter effects; periodic data; regression.
learningOutcomes: Write sinusoidal equations from features/data; interpret parameters; assess model reasonableness.

lessons.title: Tangent, Secant, Cosecant and Cotangent
subtopics: Definitions; graphs; periods; zeros; asymptotes; reciprocal relationships.
learningOutcomes: Analyze reciprocal and tangent-family functions; identify domains/asymptotes; connect graphs to sine/cosine.

lessons.title: Inverse Trigonometric Functions
subtopics: Principal values; inverse notation; solving right/general angle problems.
learningOutcomes: Evaluate inverse trig functions; solve for angles; use correct principal-value ranges.

lessons.title: Trigonometric Equations
subtopics: Solve on intervals; periodic solutions; graph/algebra methods.
learningOutcomes: Solve basic and transformed trig equations; generate all solutions on an interval; verify solutions.

lessons.title: Core Trigonometric Identities
subtopics: Reciprocal/quotient/Pythagorean; sine/cosine sum identities; simple verification.
learningOutcomes: Rewrite trig expressions; verify identities; use equivalent forms to support equation solving.

lessons.title: Polar Coordinates
subtopics: Polar grid; multiple coordinates; rectangular-polar conversion; complex-plane connection.
learningOutcomes: Plot and convert coordinates; explain multiple polar representations; connect coordinate systems.

lessons.title: Polar Graphs and Rate Language
subtopics: r=f(theta); signed radius; graphing with tables/technology; average rate of r with respect to theta.
learningOutcomes: Construct basic polar graphs; interpret signed radius; describe increasing/decreasing radius and average rate per radian.

units.title: Function Synthesis & AP Transition
units.intent: Consolidate the cross-cutting skills that distinguish students who survive AP Precalculus from students who can reason fluently in it.
units.phaseFocus: Transformations/composition/inverses; rates/covariation; model selection; regression/residuals; mixed multiple-representation reasoning.
units.implementationEvidence: Closes gaps that most often cause difficulty in AP Precalculus.

lessons.title: Transformations, Composition & Inverses Synthesis
subtopics: Mixed function families; nested functions; domain restrictions; inverse verification.
learningOutcomes: Use transformations/compositions/inverses flexibly across function families; determine valid domains; choose efficient representations.

lessons.title: Covariation and Rates Across Families
subtopics: Average rate; additive/multiplicative change; increasing/decreasing; extrema; comparison of families.
learningOutcomes: Describe how quantities change together; compare rate behavior across families; justify conclusions from multiple representations.

lessons.title: Model Selection and Regression
subtopics: Linear/quadratic/polynomial/exponential/log/sinusoidal candidates; residuals; assumptions.
learningOutcomes: Select and validate a model; interpret parameters; use residual and contextual evidence; articulate limitations.

lessons.title: AP-Style Multiple Representations
subtopics: Graph/table/formula/context translation; calculator and non-calculator tasks; concise justification.
learningOutcomes: Translate representations; sustain multi-step reasoning; communicate a mathematically valid rationale.

lessons.title: Cumulative Readiness Studio
subtopics: Mixed problems; retrieval; error analysis; targeted mini-lessons; independent practice planning.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate durable mastery; diagnose own errors; select targeted practice rather than repeating mastered content.

units.title: AP Precalculus Launch
units.intent: End Grade 10 by making the opening weeks of Grade 11 AP Precalculus familiar and manageable.
units.phaseFocus: Preview AP Topics 1.1, 1.2, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1; AP-style routines; cumulative benchmark; summer bridge plan.
units.implementationEvidence: Successful completers enter Grade 11 AP Precalculus ready to begin at AP pace.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Change in Tandem & Rates
subtopics: Preview AP 1.1-1.3; covariation; rates; multiple representations.
learningOutcomes: Enter AP Precalculus able to discuss covariation and rates precisely; solve opening-unit tasks independently.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Polynomial/Rational Reasoning
subtopics: Preview AP 1.5-1.12; zeros; end behavior; asymptotes/holes; transformations.
learningOutcomes: Connect algebraic structure to graph features; distinguish zeros/asymptotes/holes; apply transformations fluently.

lessons.title: AP Preview: Exponential/Log and Trig Thinking
subtopics: Preview AP 2.1-2.2 and 3.1; additive vs multiplicative change; periodic phenomena.
learningOutcomes: Recognize the core organizing ideas of AP Units 2 and 3; compare change patterns and periodic behavior.

lessons.title: Final AP Readiness Benchmark & Summer Bridge
subtopics: Cumulative benchmark; strand report; personalized bridge; study/technology routines.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate readiness for Grade 11 AP Precalculus; identify any summer priorities; enter the course with a concrete preparation plan.

requiredPackages.title: Gateway 1 - AP Transition Assessment
subtopics: Common core + AP-extension items; non-calculator algebra; representation translation; written rationale.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate readiness to enter AP Unit 2 pace; identify any catch-up requirements; produce clear mathematical justification.

requiredPackages.title: Gateway 2 - AP Transition Assessment
subtopics: Cumulative R1-R2 + AP-extension items; composition/inverses; modeling; written communication.
learningOutcomes: Demonstrate exceptional readiness for a midyear AP transfer or identify the exact strands to strengthen before Grade 11 AP.
